subject: pathology
title: Cervical and uterine pathology: HPV, carcinoma and leiomyoma

steps.tx: High risk human papillomavirus drives cervical cancer through viral oncoproteins. **HPV types 16 and 18** are the main high risk types, and **E6 and E7 proteins** disable p53 and Rb tumour suppressor pathways. Infection progresses through cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grades, and vaccination before exposure prevents infection with covered virus types effectively.
steps.say: High risk virus types cause cervical cancer through viral oncoprotein activity. E6 degrades p53 and E7 binds Rb in infected cervical cells. Precancer develops through intraepithelial neoplasia grades over several years progressively. Vaccination is effective because it prevents infection before exposure occurs.

steps.tx: This biopsy shows full thickness atypia of cervical squamous epithelium. The lesion is **CIN3** because atypical cells and mitoses occupy the full thickness, and the **basement membrane** remains intact with uninvaded stroma below. That intact membrane matters because it separates precancer from invasive carcinoma in examination questions.
steps.say: This section is abnormal because atypical cells occupy the full epithelial thickness. Mitoses are present high in the epithelium in this high grade lesion. The basement membrane is intact and the underlying stroma is uninvaded completely. Invasion is absent because the membrane separates precancer from carcinoma.

vis.alt: Stained cervical epithelium with atypical cells throughout thickness, annotated for CIN3 atypia, intact basement membrane and uninvaded stroma.
vis.caption: Cervical histology showing full thickness atypia with intact basement membrane. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Cervical carcinoma usually presents with abnormal bleeding and requires formal staging. **Cervical carcinoma** is most often squamous, and **FIGO staging** determines whether surgery or chemoradiation is appropriate. Early disease can be treated surgically, whereas parametrial involvement indicates advanced disease and chemoradiation is used with cisplatin based therapy.
steps.say: Cervical cancer presents with postcoital bleeding and abnormal discharge in many women. Squamous carcinoma is commonest and staging determines the correct treatment approach. Early tumours are resected surgically whereas advanced tumours receive chemoradiation instead. Parametrial spread is decisive because it changes management completely.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating the FIGO clinical staging of cervical carcinoma, showing tumor extent within the cervix, vagina, and parametrium for stages IA1, IB1, IIA, and IIB.
vis.caption: FIGO clinical staging of cervical carcinoma. Image: Edna Maite Mohuba, Tebogo Maria Mothiba, and Livhuwani Muthelo, CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma are linked to prolonged unopposed oestrogen exposure. **Atypical hyperplasia** is premalignant and requires definitive treatment, and **endometrioid carcinoma** follows PTEN loss in many cases. Serous carcinoma arises on atrophic endometrium with p53 abnormality, and postmenopausal bleeding always requires endometrial sampling for diagnosis.
steps.say: Unopposed oestrogen stimulates endometrium and it promotes hyperplasia over time progressively. Atypical hyperplasia is premalignant and hysterectomy is usually required for treatment. Endometrioid cancer presents with postmenopausal bleeding and sampling confirms the diagnosis. Serous cancer behaves aggressively because peritoneal spread occurs early.

steps.tx: Leiomyoma is a benign smooth muscle tumour that is extremely common. A **leiomyoma** causes menorrhagia and pressure symptoms, and **leiomyosarcoma** is distinguished by necrosis, atypia and increased mitoses. Adenomyosis causes a boggy tender uterus with dysmenorrhoea, whereas endometriosis causes chocolate cysts, infertility and ectopic endometrial tissue outside the uterus.
steps.say: A leiomyoma is benign and it causes heavy bleeding and pressure symptoms. Leiomyosarcoma is malignant because necrosis, atypia and mitoses are present together. Adenomyosis causes a tender boggy uterus and painful periods in affected women. Endometriosis is different because ectopic tissue causes cysts and infertility.
